title: Credential contingency & evidence automation schemata
body:
Purpose
This is a living design + runbook for credential contingency: how we vault, rotate, and perform break-glass actions while generating verifiable evidence exported to our SIEM. Focus is on RBAC v2 compatibility, audit schema to enable automated evidence ingestion, and steps for human-in-the-loop emergency access.

Scope / audience
- Primary: security engineers, SREs, on-call incident responders, compliance auditors.
- Secondary: platform engineers and solutions eng for Private/Dedicated customers who ask about evidence exports.

Quick summary (TL;DR)
- RBAC v2 roles map -> vault policies at issuance time.
- All credential lifecycle events emit a canonical audit envelope (see schema below).
- Evidence automation pipeline picks up envelopes, enriches with session metadata, and pushes to SIEM via secure collector with HMAC.
- Break-glass is strictly timeboxed, multi-ack, and emits chained signed artifacts to prove justification, approval, and post-facto rotation.

Current constraints / non-goals
- This doc does NOT redesign the vault internal store. It assumes HashiCorp Vault or equivalent KMS-backed secret store.
- Not covering customer-specific private-deployments RBAC mappings beyond pattern guidance.

Proposed audit envelope schema (plain text canonical fields for SIEM export)
- envelope_id: UUID v4
- event_ts: ISO8601 UTC
- product_component: string (e.g., "vault-agent", "rotator", "breakglass-gateway")
- actor_principal: iam:<provider>:<id> (canonicalized user/service account id)
- actor_display: human-friendly name (if present)
- action: string (issue | rotate | revoke | request_breakglass | approve_breakglass | emergency_access_start | emergency_access_end | evidence_submitted)
- target_secret_id: urn:redwood:secret:<short-id> or customer-provided id
- rbac_role_at_time: RBACv2 role identifier (e.g., role-ops-rotations)
- vault_policy_hash: sha256 of policy attached at issuance time
- justification_claim: short string provided by requester (if any)
- approval_chain: list of principal ids (comma-separated in this envelope export)
- session_nonce: short random token for session correlation
- tools: comma-separated list (e.g., cli,vault-ui,api,ssh-proxy)
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- evidence_refs: comma-separated artifact ids (signed-logs, screenshots, ticket-ids)
- signer: key-id used to sign envelope
- signature: base64 signature of canonical envelope

Note: we intentionally export a flat envelope to SIEM so index mappings are stable across customer/private instances. SIEM parsers will expand comma-separated fields into arrays where needed.

RBAC v2 -> vault policy mapping notes
- Principle: policy at issuance must be the minimum privilege for the lifetime of the credential. Map RBACv2 roles to policy templates rather than per-user policies.
- Template naming: rbacv2.template.<role_short> (e.g., rbacv2.template.ops-rotations)
- At issuance attach policy_hash and ephemeral_role_binding metadata to envelope.
- Rotation automation must reference role_template_name so post-rotation audits can verify correct policy mapping.

Break-glass flow (human readable steps)
1) Request: engineer opens SEC-EMERG ticket (JIRA SEC-####) and marks urgency and system impact. They call on-call and post a brief justification in the ticket.
2) Gate: triage on-call must acknowledge within 10 minutes and create a break-glass request object in the breakglass service.
3) Multi-ack approval: require 2 approvers from distinct teams (typically SRE lead + Security lead) OR an owner + manager if same team. Approvals recorded as signer artifacts.
4) Issuance: break-glass gateway issues an ephemeral credential with TTL <= 2 hours, with forced rotation on first use if possible. Gateway attaches justification_claim and approval_chain to the issued envelope and signs.
5) Access: session is proxied through our audit-proxy so every API call is captured and sent to the evidence collector (see pipeline below).
6) Tear-down: session_end must be recorded and a forced rotation job scheduled immediately. Evidence artifacts (signed audit log, screen capture, ticket link) are attached to envelope as evidence_refs.
7) Postmortem: create incident summary, list all secrets touched and rotations performed, and upload to Confluence.

Minimum checklists (for responders)
- Before issuing break-glass: verify ticket exists and justification is minimally adequate (what, why, impact)
- Ensure two approvers have signed; capture their userids
- Confirm ephemeral credential TTL and scope are minimal
- Turn on verbose auditing for proxied session
- After session: ensure rotation job succeeded and evidence artifacts uploaded

Evidence automation pipeline (sketch)
- collector (agent) runs alongside log-forwarder, receives audit envelopes and session chunks, signs and posts to evidence bus (internal kafka topic).
- enricher service correlates envelope with ticket, git commits, and ephemeral role bindings; it attaches derived fields (commit_ids, deployed_version).
- aggregator groups artifacts by envelope_id and writes a compact bundle to object storage (signed bundle + manifest).
- exporter sends manifest metadata to SIEM via HTTPS with mutual TLS; raw bundles retained in cold storage for 90 days (configurable per region/customer).
- retention policy: metadata to SIEM indefinitely (per compliance), raw signed bundles 90 days, rotated secrets kept as audit references but destroyed per retention policy.

SIEM export specifics / parser notes
- Use stable index: secrets-ops-audit-YYYY.MM.DD
- Export as JSON lines; one envelope per line. Keep field names exactly as above. Avoid free-form messages in top-level fields, put long text in justification_claim only.
- Example useful Kibana queries (informal):
  - "Find all breakglass events in last 7d: action:\"request_breakglass\" OR action:\"emergency_access_start\""
  - "Find rotations following breakglass: action:rotate AND exists:approval_chain"
- Recommended SIEM parsers to create: envelope_id, actor_principal (tokenize by ":"), action as keyword, tools -> keyword array, evidence_refs -> array of ids, signer -> keyword, signature -> not indexed (store only).

Inventory hygiene & rotation cadence guidance
- Inventory mode: daily incremental snapshot generated by rotator job; snapshot_id included in envelope when rotation job triggered.
- Tagging rules: every secret must have tags: owner, owner_email, product_component, created_by_role, rotation_policy_id.
- Rotation cadence default: 30 days for high-risk secrets, 90 days for standard service secrets, on-change for user secrets. Document deviations in justification_claim.

Operational runbook (quick actions)
- To trigger manual rotation for a secret: run /ops/secrets/rotate --secret <id> --snapshot <snapshot_id> --reason "post-breakglass"
- To revoke ephemeral break-glass credentials: /ops/secrets/revoke --session <session_nonce>
- To export evidence bundle for audit: /ops/evidence/export --envelope <envelope_id> --format tar.gz

Open questions / TODOs (triage for next sprint)
- Decide canonical signer key rotation cadence for envelope signer. Who owns that key? (sec-kms or infra?)
- Formalize SLA with SIEM team for export retries and error handling (backpressure on exporter).
- Decide precise retention for raw bundles in EU region for GDPR alignment.
- UX: add "why" field validation on UI to force useful justification (draft regex for useful length?).

Appendix: quick links and references
- Breakglass service: github.com/redwood-inference/breakglass (PR 42)
- Evidence collector design doc: Confluence: Evidence Automation (link above)
- RBAC v2 spec: Confluence: RBACv2 Design (internal)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally prescriptive about export schema because downstream SIEM parsers are brittle. If we change field names later we must provide a one-month dual-write window.
- Prefer feedback inline here or in PR 7812.

End of doc — working draft.
